chunks: Ibn Faddal narrated from Aban that Abu Abdullah عليه السلام said:
Regarding a man who dies as an apostate from Islam while he has children and wealth, he said: His wealth belongs to his Muslim children.

key_terms.أَوْلَادٌ: children left behind by the deceased
key_terms.لِوُلْدِهِ: for his children; indicating inheritance transfer
key_terms.مَالٌ: property or wealth owned by the deceased
key_terms.مُرْتَدًّا: one who has apostatized from Islam
key_terms.ٱلْإِسْلَامِ: the religion from which the person apostasized
key_terms.ٱلْمُسْلِمِينَ: those among his children who are Muslim

ai.seo_question: Who inherits the wealth of a person who dies as an apostate from Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the estate of a person who dies as an apostate from Islam. It states that when such a person leaves children, his wealth passes to his Muslim children, making the ruling relevant to inheritance and family financial law.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3555 - Ibn Faddal reported from Aban that Abu Abdullah (as) said:
"If a man dies as an apostate from Islam and he has children and wealth, his wealth is to be inherited by his Muslim children."
